answer: A falcon-eyed auditor then samples a meadow of candidate agents, requiring each to reveal a unique hardware fingerprint and history of real task completions. Agents must stake a bonded deposit and complete a randomized proof-of-work challenge at each epoch's zenith, where the difficulty scales with the number of new identities claiming entry. Duplicate or fabricated identities forfeit their full stake, so mass-producing sybils costs linearly more than legitimate participation ever could. From sa0023's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
